title: customers.consent-recorded.v1
description: A customer answered about one consent purpose. A withdrawal is customers.consent-withdrawn.v1, not this event with a different status, so a consumer that must honour a withdrawal immediately subscribes to exactly the fact it has to react to.
$comment: additionalProperties is true on purpose. conventions.md section 5.5 permits additive changes within a major version, so a subscriber must tolerate a field it has not seen; a closed schema would make every such addition breaking. required lists the fields present when v1 was published — a field added within v1 is optional forever, because a dead-lettered message replayed later carries the payload as it was written.

eventId.description: Identity of this occurrence. Delivery is at least once; consumers de-duplicate on it.

occurredAt.description: When the answer was recorded, in UTC.

aggregateId.description: The customer. The dispatcher never reorders this customer's committed messages, but it cannot serialise two counters answering at once: see the ordering row in docs/integration/events/README.md before relying on the order two events arrived in.

organisationId.description: The organisation the customer belongs to.

recordId.description: The consent record this event announces. Media (#31) stores it against every photograph it keeps.

purposeKey.description: The purpose, by its stable key. Renaming a purpose in the register does not change it.

status.description: What she said. Never Withdrawn, which has its own event, and never NeverAsked, which is the absence of an answer and cannot be one.

wordingVersion.description: The version of the wording she was read. A later version re-consents nobody; comparing it against the current version is how a shop finds who to ask again.

branchId.description: The branch the answer was taken at, or null where it was taken at none.

schemaVersion.description: The payload's major version. Agrees with the .v suffix of eventType.
